headline: Singer Asif Akbar's car shot at in Dhaka's Moghbazar
summary: Unknown assailants opened fire at the private car of popular singer Asif Akbar in Dhaka's Moghbazar early today. The singer escaped unharmed.
details: Unknown assailants opened fire at the private car of singer Asif Akbar in Dhaka’s Moghbazar early today. Asif escaped unharmed, said Saiful Islam, inspector (operations) of Hatirjheel Police Station.

The incident took place in front of Bishal Centre around 4:00am. Asif, who has a private office in Moghbazar, had parked his car in front of the centre. He was not inside the vehicle when the shooting took place.
Asif informed police about the incident around 5:00am. Police visited the scene following the report. No casualties were reported.

Investigators could not collect CCTV footage immediately as the shops at the market were closed. Police say they will collect the footage after the shops open and take further action based on their findings.
caption:
Gunshots fired at singer Asif Akbar's car in Dhaka's Moghbazar.

Singer Asif Akbar escaped unharmed after unknown assailants opened fire at his private vehicle early this morning.

Unknown assailants opened fire at the private car of singer Asif Akbar in Dhaka’s Moghbazar early today. Asif escaped unharmed, said Saiful Islam, inspector (operations) of Hatirjheel Police Station.

The incident took place in front of Bishal Centre around 4:00am. Asif, who has a private office in Moghbazar, had parked his car in front of the centre. He was not inside the vehicle when the shooting took place.

Asif informed police about the incident around 5:00am. Police visited the scene following the report. No casualties were reported.

Investigators could not collect CCTV footage immediately as the shops at the market were closed. Police say they will collect the footage after the shops open and take further action based on their findings.

headline: Trump warns US may carry out another military operation against Iran
summary: President Donald Trump suggests a new strike as the conflict nears eight months, while Iran prepares plans to target Gulf undersea cables.
details: President Donald Trump announced at a Florida rally that the US may launch another military operation against Iran, referring to it as another 'Epic Fury'.
The statement comes as the ongoing conflict nears its eight-month mark and rising fuel prices create pressure ahead of the US midterm elections.
Trump mentioned that while the war could end quickly, he is weighing whether to seek a swift conclusion or let the conflict wind down gradually.
He previously stated that no attack would be launched before the November 3 elections, which will determine control of the US Congress.
The conflict escalated on February 28 when the US and Israel attacked Iran, leading to retaliatory strikes on Israel and Gulf states hosting US bases.
These strikes have resulted in thousands of deaths and the displacement of millions of people across Iran, Israel, and Lebanon.
In response, senior Iranian security officials say Tehran has developed detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the US and Israel attack again.
caption:
Another 'Epic Fury'? Trump warns of new US military operations against Iran as tensions escalate.

President Donald Trump announced at a Florida rally that the US may launch another military operation against Iran, referring to it as another 'Epic Fury'.

The statement comes as the ongoing conflict nears its eight-month mark and rising fuel prices create pressure ahead of the US midterm elections.

Trump mentioned that while the war could end quickly, he is weighing whether to seek a swift conclusion or let the conflict wind down gradually.

He previously stated that no attack would be launched before the November 3 elections, which will determine control of the US Congress.

The conflict escalated on February 28 when the US and Israel attacked Iran, leading to retaliatory strikes on Israel and Gulf states hosting US bases.

These strikes have resulted in thousands of deaths and the displacement of millions of people across Iran, Israel, and Lebanon.

In response, senior Iranian security officials say Tehran has developed detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the US and Israel attack again.
